paragraphs.title: The Call to Praise the Lord

easy.q: To whom does the psalmist say, “Give unto the LORD” in verse 1?

easy.explanation: They are told to give the LORD “glory and strength.”
easy.q: What are the mighty told to give unto the LORD?

easy.explanation: Verse 2 says to “worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness.”
easy.q: How are worshippers told to worship the LORD?

answers: The glory is due unto His name
medium.explanation: The glory given to the LORD is described as being due unto His name.
medium.q: What is the relationship between the LORD’s name and the glory given to Him?

answers: Giving glory, giving strength, and worshipping in holiness
Breaking cedars, shaking wilderness, and calving hinds
medium.explanation: The verses call for giving glory and strength and for worship in holiness.

answers: The reverent splendor of holy worship
medium.explanation: The phrase describes worship marked by holiness and reverence.
medium.q: In context, what does “the beauty of holiness” most nearly describe?

answers: Even the powerful are subject to the LORD’s greatness
Only powerful people may worship the LORD
Powerful people do not need to honor God
challenge.explanation: The command shows that even the mighty must acknowledge and honor the LORD.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the command to the mighty to honor the LORD?

answers: Recognition of the LORD’s greatness and rightful authority
challenge.explanation: All three ideas point to the LORD’s greatness and the proper response of reverence.

answers: Because worship is merely a physical act
Because holiness belongs only to the wilderness
Because worship expresses deep reverence before the LORD
challenge.explanation: Holiness emphasizes the reverent and sacred character of worship.
challenge.q: Why does the psalm connect worship with holiness?

short_answers.question: According to verse 2, what is due unto the LORD’s name?
short_answers.explanation: The verse says, “Give unto the LORD the glory due unto his name.”

paragraphs.title: The Lord’s Voice in the Power of Nature

easy.explanation: The voice of the LORD is “upon the waters.”
easy.q: Where is the voice of the LORD said to be in verse 3?

easy.explanation: Verse 5 says, “The voice of the LORD breaketh the cedars.”
easy.q: What does the voice of the LORD break?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “The voice of the LORD divideth the flames of fire.”
easy.q: What does the voice of the LORD divide?

medium.explanation: The voice is called “powerful” and “full of majesty.”
medium.q: How is the voice of the LORD described in verses 3–4?

answers: Thunder, breaking cedars, shaking the wilderness, and dividing fire
medium.explanation: The passage moves through thunder, broken cedars, shaken wilderness, and divided flames.
medium.q: Which sequence best reflects the voice’s effects in this passage?

answers: A place limited to the temple
A vast setting over which the LORD’s voice resounds
medium.explanation: “Many waters” presents a broad and mighty scene for the LORD’s voice.
medium.q: What does “many waters” suggest in the description of the LORD’s voice?

answers: The LORD’s voice is limited to one place
The LORD’s voice has power throughout different parts of creation
The LORD’s voice affects plants but not the earth
challenge.explanation: The range of objects and places shows that the voice acts throughout creation.
challenge.q: What is emphasized by the voice acting upon waters, trees, fire, and wilderness?

answers: The mighty sound can recall the awe of divine revelation
The voice denies that God ever revealed Himself
The passage describes only human speech
challenge.explanation: The overwhelming voice evokes the awe associated with divine revelation.
challenge.q: What connection can be made between the thunderous voice and the revelation at Sinai?

answers: It makes the voice seem weak
It shows that only animals are affected
It portrays even great mountains as subject to the LORD’s power
challenge.explanation: The mountains’ movement demonstrates the extraordinary power of the LORD’s voice.
challenge.q: Why does the shaking of Lebanon and Sirion strengthen the passage’s message?

short_answers.question: What two words describe the voice of the LORD in verse 4?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 4 directly calls the voice “powerful” and “full of majesty.”

paragraphs.title: From Birth to Stability in the Temple

easy.explanation: Verse 9 says, “The voice of the LORD maketh the hinds to calve.”
easy.q: What does the voice of the LORD make the hinds do?

easy.explanation: The verse says that the voice “discovereth the forests.”
easy.q: What does the voice of the LORD discover?

easy.explanation: In the temple, everyone speaks of “his glory.”
easy.q: What does everyone speak of in the LORD’s temple?

answers: The voice brings forth life and exposes the forests
The voice is silent in both the wilderness and temple
The voice affects only mountains and waters
medium.explanation: The voice brings forth life through the hinds and exposes the forests.

answers: It is another place of destruction
It is a place where everyone speaks of the LORD’s glory
It is hidden beneath the forests
medium.explanation: The temple provides a setting in which the LORD’s glory is openly proclaimed.
medium.q: How does the temple relate to the upheaval in nature?

answers: Lays the forests bare or exposes them
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the forests being exposed or stripped by the LORD’s power.
medium.q: What does “discovereth the forests” most nearly mean in context?

answers: The LORD’s voice has both life-giving and disruptive effects
The LORD’s voice affects only peaceful events
The LORD’s voice has no effect on creation
challenge.explanation: The verse presents both the bringing forth of life and the upheaval of the forests.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the pairing of calving hinds and exposed forests?

answers: It shifts attention away from the LORD
It shows that the proper response to divine power is the declaration of glory
It says that nature is stronger than the temple
challenge.explanation: The temple scene turns the display of power into a communal declaration of glory.
challenge.q: How does the temple’s mention complete the description of the LORD’s voice?

answers: It separates the voice from every action
It makes the forests the main subject
It continually connects the LORD’s voice with His works in creation
challenge.explanation: The repetition emphasizes that the mighty events are caused by the LORD’s voice.
challenge.q: Why is the repeated phrase “the voice of the LORD” significant in this psalm?

paragraphs.title: The King and the Blessing of His People

easy.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD sitteth upon the flood.”
easy.q: Upon what does the LORD sit according to verse 10?

easy.explanation: The LORD sits as King “for ever.”
easy.q: How long does the LORD sit as King?

easy.explanation: The LORD gives His people strength and blesses them with peace.
easy.q: What will the LORD give unto His people?

answers: His rule over overwhelming waters and judgment
His inability to control the flood
medium.explanation: Sitting upon the flood portrays the LORD as sovereign over the waters.
medium.q: What does the LORD’s position upon the flood communicate?

answers: From the temple to the forests
From the LORD’s eternal kingship to His blessing of His people
medium.explanation: The passage moves from the LORD’s kingship to the strength and peace He gives His people.
medium.q: What movement occurs from verse 10 to verse 11?

medium.explanation: The LORD gives His people strength, meaning power or might.
medium.q: In verse 11, what does “strength” most nearly mean?

answers: The LORD brings His people from overwhelming judgment to blessing and rest
The flood continues without end for His people
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from the LORD’s rule over the flood to His gift of peace.
challenge.q: What is suggested by the movement from the flood to peace?

answers: It shows that the LORD shares His sustaining power with His people
It applies only to the cedars of Lebanon
challenge.explanation: The powerful LORD gives strength to His people as a blessing.
challenge.q: How does the gift of strength relate to the earlier description of the LORD’s voice?

answers: The LORD’s kingship ends after the flood
The eternal King gives His people strength and peace
challenge.explanation: The psalm ends by joining the LORD’s everlasting kingship with strength and peace for His people.
challenge.q: What is the final message of the psalm?

short_answers.question: What two blessings does the LORD give His people in verse 11?
short_answers.explanation: The verse says, “The LORD will give strength unto his people; the LORD will bless his people with peace.”
